Spec / why: FREE, open source. gr-iridium takes raw IQ, runs an FFT burst detector, downmixes each burst, does carrier and timing recovery, demodulates QPSK and emits bit frames; iridium-toolkit decodes them. THE POINT FOR THIS PROJECT: it reports PER-BURST FREQUENCY, so the Doppler shift is directly measurable on the ground. That replaces the 180m sigma / 2s latency model in sitl/soop_link.py with MEASURED numbers. The sigma was [A] 20m until 2026-09-04; it is now [L] 180m, the published Iridium NEXT figure without elevation aiding. 20m turned out to be the best result in the literature - four Iridium plus one Orbcomm, five satellites across two constellations, static receiver - being applied to single-constellation Iridium on a moving quad. NOTE the dominant error is EPHEMERIS, not the receiver: TLE orbit error is kilometres and is the main source of positioning inaccuracy, so no better SDR, TCXO, LNA or antenna raises the accuracy ceiling. They raise SNR, which you need to detect bursts at all.
Provenance: [D] muccc/gr-iridium README: FFT burst detect, QPSK demod, frame output

Spec / why: Nose camera recording to its own microSD. Chosen over a RunCam-class action cam because it does the same job for a fifth of the price. OV2640/OV3660 + microSD + 8MB PSRAM; with the open-source ESP32-CAM_MJPEG2SD firmware it writes ~20 fps AVI to the card (a naive JPEG-per-frame loop gets ~1 fps at SVGA - use the firmware). Takes 5V + GND from a payload pad (P41/P51/P61/P71) and nothing else: no UART, no radio. WIFI AND ESP-NOW MUST STAY OFF IN FLIGHT - the RC link is 2.4GHz ELRS and an ESP32 radiating 2.4GHz centimetres from the receiver can desensitise it, which is a control-link failure, not a video glitch. ESP-NOW cannot carry video anyway (~250 byte payloads). For LIVE video later, that is a 5.8GHz analogue AIO cam+VTX off the VBAT pad PF1 plus a UVC receiver the laptop sees as a webcam - separate purchase. Rolling shutter on a quad means jello: soft-mount it. IT CANNOT ALSO BE THE OPTICAL FLOW SENSOR, and not for one reason but four: one camera cannot face both down (flow) and forward (recording); its OV2640/OV3660 is ROLLING shutter, which prop vibration turns into jello that corrupts flow - the deferred flow camera is an OV9281 GLOBAL shutter part for exactly this reason; the sensor emits JPEG or raw, not both, and recording needs the in-sensor JPEG to stay inside the CPU budget; and SD writes stall 100ms+ during wear-levelling, which a recorder absorbs but a position-estimate loop cannot. Use a PMW3901-based module for flow - it computes flow in-sensor and needs no camera pipeline. See docs/SENSORS.md.
